title: The Global Housing Crisis Explained (English Listening Practice)
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 你好，你好，你好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 推出的《English Learning for Curious Minds》，在这里，你可以聆听精彩的故事，了解世界上奇妙而有趣的知识，同时提高你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going to be talking about the global housing crisis.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们将探讨全球住房危机。

sentences.en: All over the world, with very few exceptions, house prices have been rising, outstripping incomes, and making home ownership harder than ever before.
sentences.zh: 在世界各地，除了极少数例外，房价一直在上涨，涨幅超过了收入水平，让拥有自己的住房比以往任何时候都更加困难。

sentences.en: So in this episode, we’ll be looking at what’s actually happening, what are some of the causes and effects of this, and what–if anything–can be done about it.
sentences.zh: 因此，在本期节目中，我们将探讨实际情况、这一现象的一些起因和影响，以及我们可以采取什么措施（如果有的话）来应对它。

sentences.en: I will warn you, this is quite a long episode, but it’s an important and complicated topic, and so I hope you will excuse this being somewhat longer than usual ones.
sentences.zh: 我先提醒大家，这是一期相当长的节目，但这是一个重要且复杂的话题，所以希望大家能原谅它比平常的节目要长一些。

sentences.en: OK then, let's not waste a minute and get right into it.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们废话不多说，直接切入正题。

sentences.en: In British English, we have an expression you might not have come across before: “safe as houses”.
sentences.zh: 在英式英语中，有一个你以前可能没听过的表达：“safe as houses”。

sentences.en: Something is “safe as houses”, or “as safe as houses”.
sentences.zh: 某事是“safe as houses”，或者“as safe as houses”。

sentences.en: It’s an unusual expression, on the one hand.
sentences.zh: 从某种角度来看，这是一个很不寻常的表达。

sentences.en: Grammatically it's odd. It's 'safe as houses' [plural] even though you're describing something singular.
sentences.zh: 它的语法很奇怪。虽然你描述的是单数事物，但它用的却是复数形式的 'safe as houses'。

sentences.en: You say 'something is as safe as houses,' not 'as safe as a house.'
sentences.zh: 你会说 'something is as safe as houses'，而不是 'as safe as a house'。

sentences.en: If you had to guess what it meant, I imagine you might think “very safe”, because a house is safe, with a door and a lock, and so on.
sentences.zh: 如果你必须猜它的意思，我想你可能会认为它是“非常安全”的意思，因为房子很安全，有门、有锁等等。

sentences.en: That would be a perfectly reasonable guess, and it’s partially right.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常合理的猜测，而且它部分正确。

sentences.en: Safe as houses doesn’t just mean safe in a general sense, it typically means something is a safe and good investment.
sentences.zh: “Safe as houses”不仅仅指一般的安全，它通常意味着某事是一项安全且划算的投资。

sentences.en: After all, you can see a house. Nobody can steal your house or take it from you.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，你看得见房子。没有人能偷走你的房子或者把它从你手里抢走。

sentences.en: You can also live in it, which is something you can’t do with most investments.
sentences.zh: 你也可以住在里面，这是大多数投资做不到的。

sentences.en: And if you are lucky enough to have some extra cash and are looking for a sensible investment opportunity, historically buying property and renting it out has been considered a good option.
sentences.zh: 如果你足够幸运，手头有一些闲钱，又在寻找一个明智的投资机会，那么从历史来看，买房并把它出租一直被认为是一个不错的选择。

sentences.en: Of course this isn’t a uniquely British phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 当然，这并非英国独有的现象。

sentences.en: Investing in property is popular all over the world for similar reasons, with people in some countries tending to do it more so than others.
sentences.zh: 由于类似的原因，投资房产在世界各地都很受欢迎，有些国家的人比其他国家的人更倾向于这样做。

sentences.en: And as you may know, in the UK house prices have continued to rise almost every year, for the best part of a century.
sentences.zh: 正如你可能知道的那样，在英国，房价几乎每年都在持续上涨，持续了近一个世纪之久。

sentences.en: Slowly but surely, up and up they went. In 1952, the average price of a house in the UK was £1,891, which is the equivalent of around £48,000 today.
sentences.zh: 它们慢条斯理但坚定不移地一路走高。1952年，英国房屋的平均价格为1,891英镑，相当于今天的约48,000英镑。

sentences.en: Last year, in 2025, the average house price was £271,188.
sentences.zh: 去年，即2025年，平均房价为271,188英镑。

sentences.en: And even in inflation-adjusted terms, house prices have increased by more than five and a half times.
sentences.zh: 即使按照通货膨胀调整后的数据计算，房价也上涨了五倍半以上。

sentences.en: Now, the fact that the price has increased so drastically isn’t a terrible thing in itself.
sentences.zh: 现在，房价大幅上涨这一事实本身并不是一件可怕的事情。

sentences.en: In fact, for several decades, from the 1950s to the mid-1990s, house prices increased very gradually every year, at the same rate, more or less, as average incomes.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在几十年的时间里（从20世纪50年代到90年代中期），房价每年都在非常缓慢地上涨，涨幅大致与平均收入的增长率相当。

sentences.en: House prices went up, but so did salaries, so it all evened out.
sentences.zh: 房价上涨了，但薪水也上涨了，所以一切都平衡了。

sentences.en: Being able to buy a home on one person’s regular salary was perfectly possible.
sentences.zh: 仅凭一个人的常规薪水就能买得起房，这是完全有可能实现的。

sentences.en: But then, starting in the late 1990s, something…changed.
sentences.zh: 但随后，从20世纪90年代末开始，情况……发生了变化。

sentences.en: Instead of going up slowly but surely, property prices in the UK started to increase steeply.
sentences.zh: 英国的房价没有缓慢而坚定地上涨，而是开始急剧飙升。

sentences.en: And importantly, they started to significantly outstrip the growth in wages.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，它们的涨幅开始远远超过工资的增长。

sentences.en: In the 1950s, the average home cost the equivalent of 4 years of wages.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪50年代，一套普通住宅的价格相当于4年的工资。

sentences.en: In 2021, the average home in London cost the equivalent of almost 13 years of wages.
sentences.zh: 在2021年，伦敦的一套普通住宅价格相当于近13年的工资。

sentences.en: And rent has increased at a similar pace.
sentences.zh: 房租也以类似的速度上涨。

sentences.en: The average rent in the whole of the UK is £1,400 a month, while in London it’s a whopping £2,200.
sentences.zh: 整个英国的平均月租金为1,400英镑，而在伦敦则高达惊人的2,200英镑。

sentences.en: Now, as I’m sure you know, this is far from a uniquely British phenomenon, and the UK is not even the worst in terms of housing prices and housing affordability.
sentences.zh: 现在，正如我确信你所知道的那样，这远非英国独有的现象，而且就房价和住房负担能力而言，英国甚至还不是最糟糕的。

sentences.en: In fact, in many countries the situation is even more extreme.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在许多国家，情况甚至更加极端。

sentences.en: Cities like Sydney, Toronto, Vancouver, Hong Kong, and even in parts of Europe have all seen similar — and in some cases even sharper — rises in house prices over roughly the same period of time.
sentences.zh: 在悉尼、多伦多、温哥华、香港，甚至欧洲的一些地区，在差不多同一时期都出现了类似的房价飙升，在某些情况下涨幅甚至更加剧烈。

sentences.en: So, what’s going on? Why, almost the world over, has there been such a surge in property prices, where a roof over your head has gone from something most people could reasonably expect to afford to something that increasingly feels out of reach?
sentences.zh: 那么，到底发生了什么？为什么几乎在全世界范围内，都会出现如此巨大的房产价格飙升，以至于拥有一个遮风挡雨的家，从大多数人都能合理预期负担得起的东西，变成了一种越来越让人觉得遥不可及的事物？

sentences.en: Well, there are some unique factors that apply to specific areas, which we will go into later in the episode.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有一些适用于特定地区的独特因素，我们将在节目后面详细讨论。

sentences.en: But there are also some global forces, factors that affect the global property market.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些全球性的力量，即影响全球房地产市场的因素。

sentences.en: The first and most important shift was that buying a home gradually became less about income, and more about access to credit.
sentences.zh: 第一个也是最重要的转变是，买房逐渐不再取决于收入，而是取决于获取信贷的能力。

sentences.en: For much of the twentieth century, if you wanted to buy a house, how much you earned placed a fairly strict limit on what you could afford.
sentences.zh: 在整个20世纪的大部分时间里，如果你想买房，你的收入在很大程度上严格限制了你能买得起什么。

sentences.en: Mortgages were relatively conservative, deposits were large, interest rates were often in the double digits, and banks were cautious about how much they would lend.
sentences.zh: 房贷政策相对保守，首付很高，利率经常达到两位数，而且银行对于贷款金额也非常谨慎。

sentences.en: In other words, you couldn’t borrow very much money, and borrowing money was very expensive.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你借不到多少钱，而且借钱的成本非常高。

sentences.en: But from the late 1990s onwards, borrowing became easier and cheaper.
sentences.zh: 但从20世纪90年代末开始，借贷变得更容易、更便宜了。

sentences.en: Interest rates fell, not just in the UK, but across much of the developed world.
sentences.zh: 不仅在英国，在整个发达世界的大部分地区，利率都在下降。

sentences.en: Monthly mortgage payments became more affordable.
sentences.zh: 每月需要偿还的房贷变得更容易负担了。

sentences.en: And banks became increasingly willing to lend larger multiples of people’s incomes.
sentences.zh: 银行也越来越愿意提供相当于人们收入更高倍数的贷款。

sentences.en: This had a powerful effect on prices. It pushed them up dramatically.
sentences.zh: 这对房价产生了强大的影响。它把房价戏剧性地推高了。

sentences.en: Estate agents increasingly encouraged prospective buyers to think not about the sale price, but rather the monthly mortgage payments.
sentences.zh: 房地产中介越来越鼓励潜在买家不要去想售价，而是去关注每月的房贷还款额。

sentences.en: After all, if your monthly payments are affordable, the price of your house is just a number; it doesn’t really matter.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，如果你的月供负担得起，房子的总价就只是个数字；它其实没那么重要。

sentences.en: And anyway, it would almost certainly go up.
sentences.zh: 而且无论如何，它几乎肯定会涨的。

sentences.en: They always did. As long as interest rates stayed low, house prices were allowed to keep climbing.
sentences.zh: 它们以前总是会涨。只要利率保持低位，房价就会一直攀升。

sentences.en: And, like with anything, the more prices rose, the more attractive property became as an investment opportunity.
sentences.zh: 而且，像所有事物一样，价格涨得越高，房产作为投资机会就越有吸引力。

sentences.en: For many years, it was very attractive, in the UK especially, which had all sorts of incentives encouraging people to become landlords.
sentences.zh: 多年来，房产极具吸引力，特别是在英国，这里有各种各样的激励措施鼓励人们成为房东。

sentences.en: After all, the bank would only require a small deposit, a tenant’s monthly rent would more than cover the monthly mortgage costs, and the price would continue to rise.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，银行只需要少量的首付，租客每月的租金就足以支付每月的房贷成本，而且房价还会继续上涨。

sentences.en: What this meant was that housing increasingly stopped being treated primarily as a place to live, and started being treated as a financial asset.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，住房越来越不再被主要视作一个居住的地方，而是开始被视作一项金融资产。

sentences.en: Then, of course, came the Great Financial Crisis of 2008.
sentences.zh: 当然，随之而来的是2008年的全球金融危机。

sentences.en: This crisis, which began with risky mortgages in the United States, showed what could happen when housing prices became completely disconnected from economic fundamentals.
sentences.zh: 这场始于美国高风险抵押贷款的危机，展现了当房价与经济基本面完全脱节时会发生什么。

sentences.en: As you'll know, when the bubble burst, millions of people lost their homes, banks collapsed, and the global economy went into freefall.
sentences.zh: 正如你所知，当泡沫破裂时，数百万人失去了家园，银行倒闭，全球经济陷入自由落体式衰退。

sentences.en: You might think this would have taught everyone a lesson.
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为这会给所有人上一课。

sentences.en: That it might have led to a complete rethink of housing as an investment vehicle.
sentences.zh: 这可能会促使人们对作为投资工具的住房进行彻底的反思。

sentences.en: But what actually happened was, in many ways, the opposite.
sentences.zh: 但实际发生的情况在很多方面恰恰相反。

sentences.en: Governments and central banks were absolutely terrified of another collapse.
sentences.zh: 政府和中央银行对又一次崩盘感到无比恐惧。

sentences.en: So instead of allowing prices to fall to more affordable levels, they did everything in their power to support the market and prevent prices from dropping too far.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了不让房价跌回更具可负担性的水平，他们竭尽全力支撑市场，防止价格跌得太深。

sentences.en: They pumped lots of money into the financial system, and kept interest rates extremely low, for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 他们向金融系统注入了大量资金，并将利率保持在极低水平，而且持续了很长时间。

sentences.en: In some countries, rates stayed close to zero for more than a decade.
sentences.zh: 在一些国家，利率接近零的水平持续了十多年之久。

sentences.en: The aim was to make borrowing cheap, encourage spending, and keep economies alive.
sentences.zh: 这样做的目的是降低借贷成本，鼓励消费，并维持经济运转。

sentences.en: And in many ways, it worked. The world bounced back.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，它确实起作用了。世界经济复苏了。

sentences.en: But there was a side effect. A huge inflow of capital into assets: stocks, bonds, and crucially, property.
sentences.zh: 但也有一个副作用。大量资本流入了资产市场：股票、债券，最关键的是，房地产。

sentences.en: And this is where the idea of housing as a global market starts to make a little more sense.
sentences.zh: 正是在这里，“将住房视为全球市场”这个概念开始变得更容易理解了。

sentences.en: In the past, the price of a home was mostly determined by local factors: local wages, local demand, local supply, because the people buying and living in them would be locals.
sentences.zh: 过去，房屋的价格主要由当地因素决定：当地工资、当地需求、当地供应，因为买房和居住在那里的人都是当地人。

sentences.en: But increasingly, housing prices were being influenced by global money.
sentences.zh: 但渐渐地，房价开始受到全球资金的影响。

sentences.en: Money looking for safety. Money looking for returns.
sentences.zh: 寻找安全港的资金。寻找回报的资金。

sentences.en: And this money isn’t abstract. It comes from pension funds, insurance companies, investment firms, and wealthy individuals, all looking for places to park large sums of money in assets that feel stable and predictable.
sentences.zh: 而且这些资金并不是抽象的。它们来自养老基金、保险公司、投资公司和富裕个人，他们都在寻找地方将巨额资金投入到感觉稳定且可预测的资产中。

sentences.en: Compared to complex financial products, housing looks reassuringly simple.
sentences.zh: 与复杂的金融产品相比，住房看起来简单得让人安心。

sentences.en: It exists physically. It generates income through rent.
sentences.zh: 它有实体存在。它通过租金产生收入。

sentences.en: And governments have a strong incentive to stop its value from collapsing.
sentences.zh: 而且政府有强烈的动机去阻止其价值崩盘。

sentences.en: And once housing becomes part of that global flow of capital, it stops behaving like an ordinary good.
sentences.zh: 一旦住房成为全球资本流动的一部分，它就不再表现得像普通商品了。

sentences.en: At that point, it doesn’t really matter whether a flat is in London, Lisbon, or Toronto.
sentences.zh: 在那一点上，一套公寓究竟是在伦敦、里斯本还是多伦多，其实已经不重要了。

sentences.en: What matters is that it’s in a country with a stable legal system, strong property rights, and a reputation for safety.
sentences.zh: 重要的是它位于一个拥有稳定法律体系、强大财产权且以安全著称的国家。

sentences.en: That’s why similar patterns started to appear in very different places; a fireman in Paris was now no longer bidding for a property against the local greengrocer, schoolteacher, and wedding photographer, but against sophisticated international investors.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么非常不同的地方开始出现类似的模式；巴黎的一名消防员现在不再是与当地的蔬菜商、学校老师和婚礼摄影师竞拍房产，而是与成熟的国际投资者竞争。

sentences.en: So, demand for housing soon started to significantly outstrip supply in most major cities, further pushing up prices.
sentences.zh: 因此，在大多数主要城市，住房需求很快开始大大超过供给，进一步推高了房价。

sentences.en: Now, the obvious question is, “if demand is so high, why don't we just build more houses?”
sentences.zh: 现在，显而易见的问题是，“如果需求这么高，为什么我们不直接多建一些房子呢？”

sentences.en: This is where we need to talk about housing supply.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们需要讨论住房供应的地方。

sentences.en: Because alongside all these financial factors pushing up prices, there's also been a chronic failure to build enough housing where people actually want to live.
sentences.zh: 因为除了所有这些推高价格的金融因素之外，还有一个长期存在的顽疾，那就是未能在他人们真正想住的地方建造足够的住房。

sentences.en: In the UK, the planning system is notoriously complex and restrictive.
sentences.zh: 在英国，规划系统出了名的复杂且限制重重。

sentences.en: Getting permission to build can take years, and even when permission is granted, local opposition often delays or blocks development entirely.
sentences.zh: 获得建设许可可能需要数年时间，甚至在获得许可后，当地的反对意见往往也会延迟或彻底阻止开发。

sentences.en: There's actually an acronym for this: NIMBY, which stands for "Not In My Back Yard", and describes someone who opposes new construction in their area, worried it will change the character of the neighbourhood or reduce their own property values.
sentences.zh: 其实对此有一个缩写词：NIMBY，代表“Not In My Back Yard”（不要在我家后院），用来形容那些反对在其所在地区进行新建设的人，他们担心这会改变社区的面貌或降低他们自己的房产价值。

sentences.en: And then there are the practical constraints.
sentences.zh: 然后还有现实中的限制因素。

sentences.en: You can't build more land in central London, or San Francisco, or Hong Kong.
sentences.zh: 你无法在伦敦市中心、旧金山或香港凭空造出更多的土地。

sentences.en: These cities are hemmed in by geography, and the most desirable areas are already built up.
sentences.zh: 这些城市受地理条件限制，最理想的区域已经完全开发完毕了。

sentences.en: Add to this rising construction costs, labour shortages, and the fact that developers sometimes hold onto land rather than building on it—hoping values will increase even further—and you have a situation where supply simply can't keep up with demand.
sentences.zh: 再加上不断上涨的建筑成本、劳动力短缺，以及开发商有时囤地不建（希望土地价值进一步上涨）这一事实，这就导致了一种供应根本无法跟上需求的局面。

sentences.en: So even if the money side of things were sorted out, we'd still have a fundamental shortage of homes in the places where people actually want to live.
sentences.zh: 因此，即使金融层面的问题得到了解决，在人们真正想居住的地方，我们依然会面临根本性的住房短缺。

sentences.en: And demand keeps growing. Not just from population growth, but from changing demographics.
sentences.zh: 而且需求还在持续增长。不仅仅是因为人口增长，还因为人口统计结构的变化。

sentences.en: People are living longer. More people are living alone.
sentences.zh: 人们活得更久了。独居的人越来越多了。

sentences.en: In much of the developed world, the average household size has been shrinking for decades, which means you need more units of housing for the same number of people.
sentences.zh: 在发达世界的大部分地区，平均家庭规模几十年来一直在缩减，这意味着同样数量的人口需要更多的住房单元。

sentences.en: Add to this an increasing number of people, both domestically and internationally, migrating into cities, and you have even more pressure on the housing supply.
sentences.zh: 再加上国内和国际上有越来越多的民众向城市迁移，这给住房供应带来了更大的压力。

sentences.en: All these factors mean that even maintaining current affordability would require building significantly more homes than we currently do.
sentences.zh: 所有这些因素意味着，即便只是维持当前的住房可负担性，也需要建造比目前多得多的房屋。

sentences.en: So, prices are almost guaranteed to rise.
sentences.zh: 因此，房价几乎注定要上涨。

sentences.en: This isn’t just speculation or financial engineering, it’s basic arithmetic.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是投机或是金融工程，这是基本的算术。

sentences.en: More people competing for the same number of homes pushes up both rents and prices, regardless of how sensible or well-intentioned housing policy might be.
sentences.zh: 更多的人竞争相同数量的房屋，这会把租金和房价同时推高，无论住房政策有多明智或出于多好的善意。

sentences.en: And there is more. Just when it seemed like low interest rates might last forever, everything changed again.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此。正当低利率似乎要永远持续下去的时候，一切又变了。

sentences.en: In 2022, inflation came roaring back. Central banks, which had spent over a decade keeping rates at historic lows, suddenly had to do a u-turn.
sentences.zh: 2022年，通货膨胀卷土重来。花了一个多世纪把利率维持在历史低位的中央银行，突然不得不来个大转弯。

sentences.en: In a matter of months, interest rates went from near zero to levels not seen in over a decade.
sentences.zh: 在几个月内，利率从接近零飙升到了十多年未见的水平。

sentences.en: In the UK, the base rate went from 0.1% to 5%.
sentences.zh: 在英国，基准利率从0.1%飙升至5%。

sentences.en: In the United States, rates rose even faster.
sentences.zh: 在美国，利率上升的速度甚至更快。

sentences.en: For anyone with a mortgage, this was a shock.
sentences.zh: 对于任何背负房贷的人来说，这都是一个打击。

sentences.en: If your rate wasn’t fixed, your monthly payments soared.
sentences.zh: 如果你的利率不是固定的，你的月供就会猛增。

sentences.en: People who had borrowed the maximum amount when rates were 2% suddenly found themselves paying twice as much each month.
sentences.zh: 那些在利率为2%时借了最高额度贷款的人，突然发现自己每月的还款额翻了一番。

sentences.en: You might have thought this would have led to a fall in house prices, as people wouldn’t have been able to borrow as much as before.
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为这会导致房价下跌，因为人们将无法像以前那样借到那么多钱。

sentences.en: But here's the thing: house prices didn't collapse.
sentences.zh: 但事实是：房价并没有崩盘。

sentences.en: They did fall slightly in some areas, and sales slowed down dramatically.
sentences.zh: 它们在某些地区确实略有下跌，销售也急剧放缓。

sentences.en: But prices remained stubbornly high. Why?
sentences.zh: 但房价依然顽固地保持在高位。为什么？

sentences.en: Well, because many people who already owned homes simply stayed put.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为许多已经拥有住房的人干脆选择按兵不动。

sentences.en: If you had a cheap mortgage locked in, selling rarely made sense — because wherever you moved next would almost certainly come with a much more expensive loan.
sentences.zh: 如果你锁定了一个便宜的房贷，卖房往往毫无意义——因为无论你搬到哪里，接下来的新贷款几乎肯定会贵得多。

sentences.en: This created a kind of gridlock. Not enough homes for sale, still too expensive for first-time buyers to afford, but with even higher monthly costs due to expensive mortgages.
sentences.zh: 这就造成了一种僵局。没有足够的房屋出售，对于首次购房者来说依然贵得买不起，但由于房贷成本高昂，每月的开销甚至变得更高了。

sentences.en: In other words, the problem got worse, not better.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，问题变得更严重了，而不是有所改善。

sentences.en: So by this point, housing is being pulled in several directions at once: cheap money pushing prices up, global capital treating homes as assets, more people competing for housing in the same cities, and a system that struggles to build enough homes where they’re needed.
sentences.zh: 所以到目前为止，住房市场正同时受到多股力量的拉扯：廉价资金将房价推高，全球资本将住宅视为资产，更多人在相同的城市中竞争住房，以及一个在需要的地方很难建造足够住房的系统。

sentences.en: And these are often exacerbated, made worse, by specific local conditions, so let’s talk about some of those now.
sentences.zh: 而且这些情况往往因具体的当地条件而进一步恶化、雪上加霜，所以我们现在来谈谈其中一些情况。

sentences.en: Particularly in Europe, and in almost any reasonably sized city, an oft-cited culprit is short-term rentals, and one name in particular coming to mind: Airbnb.
sentences.zh: 特别是在欧洲，在几乎任何一个像样大小的城市里，一个经常被归咎的罪魁祸首就是短期租赁，其中有一个名字尤其让人印象深刻：Airbnb。

sentences.en: Landlords were choosing not to rent out their apartments long-term to locals, but to tourists on a short-term basis.
sentences.zh: 房东们选择不把公寓长期租给当地人，而是以短期形式租给游客。

sentences.en: The economic rationale for this is pretty obvious; a landlord can typically make much more money.
sentences.zh: 背后的经济逻辑相当明显；房东通常能赚到更多钱。

sentences.en: But the effect on the local property market, as no doubt many of you will know all too well, is that it has reduced the supply of available housing for locals and significantly pushed up prices, both to buy and to rent.
sentences.zh: 但正如你们当中的许多人可能非常清楚的那样，它对当地房地产市场产生的影响是，它减少了当地人可获得的住房供应，并大幅推高了购买和租赁的价格。

sentences.en: In Madrid and Barcelona, for example, over the past decade, rents have risen by an average of 60% and prices by 90%.
sentences.zh: 例如，在马德里和巴塞罗那，过去十年中，租金平均上涨了60%，房价上涨了90%。

sentences.en: And then there are the countries which courted wealthy foreigners with citizenship or tax incentives on the condition that they invested in property.
sentences.zh: 然后还有一些国家，它们通过提供公民身份或税收优惠来讨好富裕外国人，条件是他们要在当地投资房地产。

sentences.en: In Malta, the tiny Mediterranean island where I used to live, citizenship was given to foreigners on the condition they bought property over a certain value, thereby reducing the housing supply for locals and pushing up prices.
sentences.zh: 在马耳他，这个我曾经居住过的小型地中海岛国，外国人在购买超过一定价值的房产的条件下可以获得公民身份，从而减少了当地人的住房供应并推高了房价。

sentences.en: On the other side of Europe, Portugal had a similar scheme which offered residency to people investing in the local property market.
sentences.zh: 在欧洲的另一端，葡萄牙也有类似的计划，为投资当地房地产市场的人提供居留权。

sentences.en: In both of these cases, these policies successfully attracted lots of foreign money that would otherwise not have come, but it also helped push up prices to unprecedented levels.
sentences.zh: 在这两种情况下，这些政策都成功地吸引了大量本不会流入的外国资金，但也助长了房价飙升至空前的高度。

sentences.en: In Malta, property prices have doubled in the past decade.
sentences.zh: 在马耳他，房价在过去十年中翻了一番。

sentences.en: The average asking price in Malta is €414,000, yet the average salary is under €25,000.
sentences.zh: 马耳他的平均挂牌价为414,000欧元，然而平均薪水却不到25,000欧元。

sentences.en: And it’s a similar situation in Portugal.
sentences.zh: 葡萄牙的情况也类似。

sentences.en: In places like this, home ownership for anyone without family help is now something of a pipe dream.
sentences.zh: 在这些地方，任何没有家庭资助的人想要拥有自己的住房，现在简直就像是天方夜谭。

sentences.en: And this brings us to one of the most insidious effects: housing wealth is becoming hereditary.
sentences.zh: 这就给我们带来了最阴险的影响之一：住房财富正在变成世袭的。

sentences.en: Increasingly, the only way young people can afford to buy is with help from parents - money for a deposit, co-signing mortgages, sometimes buying outright.
sentences.zh: 越来越明显的是，年轻人唯一买得起房子的途径就是得到父母的帮助——提供首付资金、共同签署房贷，有时甚至直接买断。

sentences.en: If your parents own property, you might still get on the ladder, as the expression goes.
sentences.zh: 如果你的父母拥有房产，正如俗话所说，你或许还能挤上这趟阶梯。

sentences.en: If they don't, you're locked out, regardless of how hard you work.
sentences.zh: 如果他们没有，无论你工作多么努力，你都会被拒之门外。

sentences.en: It means your ability to own a home depends less on your income than on whether you were lucky enough to have parents who bought property decades ago when it was still affordable.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你拥有住房的能力，与其说取决于你的收入，不如说取决于你是否足够幸运，拥有在几十年前房价还算负担得起时买房的父母。

sentences.en: So this is the picture so far. Global forces push prices up everywhere.
sentences.zh: 这就是目前的整体图景。全球力量在各地推高房价。

sentences.en: Local factors make the problem worse in certain places.
sentences.zh: 局部因素在某些地方使问题进一步恶化。

sentences.en: And once prices reach a certain level, you get the situation that exists in many towns and cities all over the world today.
sentences.zh: 一旦价格达到某个水平，你就会看到今天世界上许多城镇和城市中存在的这种局面。

sentences.en: Whether it’s paying sky-high rent or not being able to afford a deposit for your first home, just having your own roof over your head is more expensive than ever.
sentences.zh: 无论是支付极高的房租，还是买不起第一套房子的首付，仅仅拥有一个属于自己的遮风挡雨之所都比以往任何时候都要昂贵。

sentences.en: So, this brings us to the trickiest part of the story.
sentences.zh: 因此，这就把我们带到了这个故事中最棘手的部分。

sentences.en: What, if anything can be done about it? It’s a problem that lots of people like to see easy solutions to.
sentences.zh: 我们能对它做些什么（如果有的话）？这是一个许多人希望看到简单解决方案的问题。

sentences.en: Build more homes, control rents, tax speculation, restrict short-term rentals, and stop prices from rising so fast.
sentences.zh: 建造更多的房屋、控制租金、对投机行为征税、限制短期租赁，并阻止房价如此迅速地上涨。

sentences.en: The reality is that all of these solutions come with their own share of problems.
sentences.zh: 现实情况是，所有这些解决方案本身都伴随着各自的问题。

sentences.en: Building takes time, and in many countries–especially in the UK–it is fraught with regulations.
sentences.zh: 建设需要时间，而在许多国家（尤其是英国），它充满了各种法规限制。

sentences.en: Removing planning constraints sounds simple, but in practice it rarely is.
sentences.zh: 取消规划限制听起来很简单，但在实践中却很少如此。

sentences.en: Rent control is one of the most debated solutions.
sentences.zh: 租金管制是争论最多的解决方案之一。

sentences.en: The idea is simple: cap how much landlords can increase rent each year, making housing more affordable for tenants.
sentences.zh: 这个想法很简单：限制房东每年提高租金的幅度，让租客更能负担得起住房。

sentences.en: But in practice, it's complicated. Economists often point to cities like San Francisco or Stockholm, where strict rent control led to some landlords taking properties off the rental market entirely, either selling them or leaving them empty.
sentences.zh: 但在实践中，这很复杂。经济学家经常以旧金山或斯德哥尔摩等城市为例，在这些城市，严厉的租金管制导致一些房东完全将房产撤出租赁市场，要么将其售出，要么任由其空置。

sentences.en: This creates a paradox: by trying to make rent cheaper for some, it often makes it harder for others to find a home at all.
sentences.zh: 这就产生了一个悖论：通过试图让一部分人的租金变得更便宜，它往往让其他人更难找到住处。

sentences.en: That said, some cities have found some middle ground.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，一些城市也找到了一些折中的平衡点。

sentences.en: Berlin tried strict rent controls, had to partially reverse them, but maintained some protections.
sentences.zh: 柏林尝试过严格的租金管制，不得不部分撤回，但保留了一些保护措施。

sentences.en: The key seems to be balancing tenant protection with incentives to keep landlords in the market.
sentences.zh: 关键似乎在于平衡租客保护与激励房东留在市场上的动力。

sentences.en: It's not a silver bullet, but it's not entirely useless either.
sentences.zh: 它不是万灵药，但也并非完全没用。

sentences.en: Restricting short-term rentals is something many cities have now started to do, with some success, but there are question marks about how deep an effect this will have on revenue from tourism.
sentences.zh: 限制短期租赁是许多城市现在已经开始做的事情，并取得了一定的成功，但对于这会对旅游业收入产生多深远的影响，仍然存在疑问。

sentences.en: Taxing speculation is a nice idea in theory, but it quickly comes up against another uncomfortable reality: homeowners, who in many countries make up a majority of the voting population, have a vested interest in prices not coming down, especially if they took on a large mortgage.
sentences.zh: 对投机征税在理论上是个好主意，但它很快就会遭遇另一个令人不安的现实：在许多国家构成投票人口大多数的房东们，与房价不下跌有着切身利益，特别是如果他们背负了巨额房贷的话。

sentences.en: For millions of people, their home isn’t just somewhere to live.
sentences.zh: 对于数百万普通人来说，他们的家不仅仅是一个居住的地方。

sentences.en: It’s their main asset. A large part of their retirement plan.
sentences.zh: 它是他们主要的资产。是他们退休计划中的很大一部分。

sentences.en: Their financial safety net. So when house prices rise, homeowners feel richer and more secure.
sentences.zh: 是他们的财务安全网。因此，当房价上涨时，房东会觉得更富有、更安全。

sentences.en: But when prices fall — or even stop rising — the same group feels threatened.
sentences.zh: 但当房价下跌——甚至停止上涨时——同一群人就会感到受到威胁。

sentences.en: So, governments face a dilemma. On the one hand, high house prices lock younger people out of home ownership, increase inequality, and put pressure on rents.
sentences.zh: 因此，政府面临着两难境地。一方面，高房价把年轻人挡在了购房门槛之外，加剧了不平等，并给租金带来了压力。

sentences.en: On the other hand, falling house prices risk angering existing homeowners and losing voters, destabilising banks, and triggering wider economic problems.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，下跌的房价有可能激怒现有的房东并流失选民、破坏银行稳定，并引发更广泛的经济问题。

sentences.en: So instead of dramatic reform, what we often see are small, cautious adjustments, adjustments that don’t always have the intended consequences.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们往往看到的不是激进的改革，而是小幅、谨慎的调整，而这些调整并不总是能产生预期的后果。

sentences.en: Governments announce ambitious plans to build more homes, like the new Labour government did in the UK, but planning slows down everything, and they quickly miss their targets.
sentences.zh: 政府宣布了雄心勃勃的建房计划，就像英国的新工党政府所做的那样，但规划拖慢了一切，他们很快就无法达标了。

sentences.en: They launch initiatives to help first-time buyers with interest-free loans, but these often end up pushing prices higher by increasing demand.
sentences.zh: 他们推出了通过免息贷款帮助首次购房者的倡议，但这些措施最终往往通过增加需求把房价推得更高。

sentences.en: They talk about controlling rents, but make promises to potential investors that their rights will also be protected.
sentences.zh: 他们谈论控制租金，但又向潜在投资者做出承诺，保证他们的权利也会得到保护。

sentences.en: They make pledges to crack down on Airbnb, but all that happens is the implementation of token "tourist taxes".
sentences.zh: 他们承诺严厉打击 Airbnb，但实际发生的却只是实施了象征性的“旅游税”。

sentences.en: And then there’s the issue of timing. Even if a government decides today to build significantly more housing, the effects won’t be felt for several years.
sentences.zh: 然后还有时机的问题。即便政府今天决定大幅增加住房建设，其效果也要在几年后才能显现出来。

sentences.en: Planning, the actual construction, building in places where people actually want to live.
sentences.zh: 规划、实际施工、在人们真正想住的地方进行建设。

sentences.en: That all takes time. So where does that leave us?
sentences.zh: 这一切都需要时间。那么这把我们置于何地呢？

sentences.en: Can house prices keep rising faster than incomes indefinitely?
sentences.zh: 房价能无限期地以快于收入的速度继续上涨吗？

sentences.en: The optimistic view is that they can't. At some point, prices must correct, either through a crash or through a long period of stagnation while wages gradually catch up.
sentences.zh: 乐观的看法是它们不能。在某个时刻，房价必须进行修正，要么通过市场崩盘，要么通过长期的停滞期，直到工资逐渐赶上来。

sentences.en: The pessimistic view is that we're not in a traditional bubble waiting to pop.
sentences.zh: 悲观的看法是，我们并不是身处一个等待破裂的传统泡沫中。

sentences.en: This is, as they say, a new equilibrium.
sentences.zh: 正如他们所说，这是一种新的平衡状态。

sentences.en: As long as housing is seen as one of the safest places to park wealth, as long as there's more capital looking for safe returns than there are good investment opportunities, as long as people continue to move to towns and cities, and as long as we don't build enough homes in desirable locations, prices will keep climbing.
sentences.zh: 只要住房被视为藏匿财富最安全的地方之一，只要寻找安全回报的资本多于好的投资机会，只要人们继续向城镇和城市迁移，只要我们没有在理想的地点建造足够的房屋，价格就会继续攀升。

sentences.en: The truth is probably somewhere in between, and will vary by location.
sentences.zh: 真相可能介于两者之间，并且会因地理位置而异。

sentences.en: Some markets may see corrections. Others may plateau, or even continue to rise.
sentences.zh: 一些市场可能会看到调整。其他市场可能会趋于平稳，甚至继续上涨。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, it seems that the fundamental tension between housing as a human necessity and housing as a financial asset is here to stay.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，作为人类必需品的住房与作为金融资产的住房之间根本性的紧张关系，似乎将长期存在。

sentences.en: OK, then, that is it for today's episode on the global property crisis.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天的全球房地产危机专题节目就到这里。

sentences.en: As always, I would love to know what you thought of this episode.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我很想听听你对这期节目的看法。

sentences.en: How have property prices changed in your city?
sentences.zh: 你所在城市的房价发生了怎样的变化？

sentences.en: How has this affected your life, and what do you think can be done about it?
sentences.zh: 这如何影响了你的生活，你认为可以为此做些什么？

sentences.en: For the members among you, you can head right into our community forum, which is at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 对于会员朋友们，你可以直接进入我们的社区论坛，网址是 community.leonardoenglish.com，与其他充满好奇心的朋友们畅所欲言。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你刚才收听的是由 Leonardo English 推出的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，祝你一切安全，我们下期节目再见。
